classification_scheme.Directly supportable: GSMA KG contains a closely corresponding concept, mechanism, or relationship for this fault type.
classification_scheme.Mechanism-level support: KG and/or primary 3GPP specification supports the underlying telecom mechanism, but not an explicit fault-label entity.

relation_type_definitions.governed-by: The KPI behavior or fault mechanism is defined and regulated by this 3GPP clause.
relation_type_definitions.specified-in: The procedure, component, or scheduling behavior causing the fault is specified in this clause.
relation_type_definitions.measured-by: The KPI affected by this fault is formally defined and measured per this clause.

shap_update_note: affected_kpis in every row will be populated with SHAP-ranked channel values from the trained Random Forest classifier in Week 7. SHAP updating does not alter the underlying 3GPP/O-RAN alignment unless subsequent standards validation identifies a correction.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §4.2.1 (BS type 1-C conducted requirement reference points; antenna connector) + TS 38.141-1 §7.2 (Reference sensitivity level)
rows.clause_text: §4.2.1: 'The conducted requirements for BS type 1-C are specified at the BS antenna connector.' §7.2 defines the reference sensitivity level as the minimum mean power applied to each antenna connector at which the throughput requirement shall be met.
rows.causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Antenna functions, RF transmission, and receiver chains are physically located at the O-RU. Antenna failure is a hardware fault at the radio unit layer.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains AAS BS, antenna array, composite antenna, receiver RF requirements, transmitter characteristics, and OTA co-location requirements from TS 38.141-1 and TS 38.104. TS 38.141-1 §4.2.1 explicitly defines the BS antenna connector reference point and shows external TX/RX filter paths.
rows.notes: Upgraded from §4 (too broad) to §4.2.1 + §7.2 (specific subclauses confirmed in Rel-19 V19.3.0). These clauses provide mechanism-level RF evidence rather than an explicit 'antenna failure' fault definition.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §6.1.3.1 (Buffer Status Report MAC CEs — Short BSR, Long BSR, Extended BSR, Truncated BSR formats) + TS 38.321 §5.4 (BSR procedure)
rows.clause_text: §6.1.3.1 defines the Buffer Status Report MAC Control Elements including Short BSR, Long BSR, Short Truncated BSR, Long Truncated BSR, and Extended Long BSR formats. §5.4 defines the BSR procedure governing when and how the UE reports buffer status to the gNB.
rows.causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler responsible for uplink PRB allocation and BSR processing runs in the O-DU. Buffer overflow is a scheduling/resource allocation failure at the O-DU layer.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains Buffer Status Report as a MAC control element, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, RLC buffer Payload, and soft buffer from TS 38.321 and TS 38.523.
rows.notes: Upgraded from §6.1.3 (too broad) to §6.1.3.1 + §5.4. Support class correctly retained at Mechanism-level: BSR ≠ buffer overflow.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.8 (In-channel selectivity — defines receiver performance under co-channel interference conditions)
rows.clause_text: §7.8 In-channel selectivity: defines the receiver's ability to receive a wanted signal in the presence of a co-channel interfering signal. Includes subsections for definition and applicability, minimum requirement, test purpose, test method, and test requirements.
rows.causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Co-channel interference is a physical-layer RF phenomenon occurring at the receive chain of the O-RU.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains in-device coexistence interference, IDC assistance information, in-channel selectivity, co-location blocking, guardband, minimum guardband, SINR-related measurements, and Zero Forcing from TS 38.141-1 and TS 38.104.
rows.notes: §7.8 confirmed as In-channel selectivity in Rel-19 V19.3.0. Mild and Severe share the same governing clause — the distinction is in TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not in the 3GPP specification.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.8 (In-channel selectivity) + TS 38.104 §4.9 (OTA co-location with other base stations; requirements ensuring co-located systems operate with minimal mutual degradation)
rows.clause_text: §7.8: same as Mild CCI row. TS 38.104 §4.9: defines OTA co-location requirements specifying the conditions under which co-located base stations shall operate without causing unacceptable mutual interference.
rows.causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Severe CCI remains a physical-layer RF phenomenon at the O-RU receive chain. The Near-RT RIC may be involved in interference mitigation response via xApp, but the primary component experiencing the fault is the O-RU.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP; O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC E2 interface for interference management xApp response)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: Same KG evidence as Mild CCI plus TX IMD co-location requirements and out-of-band blocking co-location requirements from TS 38.104 §4.9.
rows.notes: TS 38.104 §4.9 description reworded — it does not define 'severe CCI'; it specifies co-location mutual interference requirements. Severity is TelecomTS-defined.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: 3GPP TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler; channel model and mobility-related propagation effects) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility/Doppler formulation) [secondary mechanism reference]
rows.clause_text: Pending PDF confirmation of TR 38.901 Rel-19 V19.1.0. §7.6.6 is expected to define the time-varying channel model including Doppler frequency shift as a function of UE velocity. §7.6.10 is expected to cover dual mobility scenarios. To be confirmed and replaced with direct quote.
rows.pdf_action_required: Confirm TR 38.901 Rel-19 V19.1.0 §7.6.6 and §7.6.10 cover time-varying Doppler frequency and channel aging. Source: https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_TR/138900_138999/138901/19.01.00_60/tr_138901v190100p.pdf
rows.causal_mechanism: High UE velocity causes rapid channel variation (channel aging) between channel estimation and data transmission. By the time precoding and MCS selection are applied based on the estimated channel state, the channel has changed significantly. This mismatch causes DL_MCS to be selected too optimistically, resulting in elevated UL_BLER and declining UL_SNR as retransmissions accumulate. Distinguished from interference-based faults by the correlation with UE mobility.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
rows.notes: Primary reference changed from TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (unconfirmed) to TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10. clause_text and pdf_action_required retained until PDF is confirmed.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.133 §4.3.5 (Relative Time Stamp Accuracy for Radio Link Failure and Handover Failure Log Reporting) + TS 38.331 RRC handover configuration and procedure clauses
rows.clause_text: TS 38.133 §4.3.5: 'This clause specifies the requirements for Relative Time Stamp Accuracy for Radio Link Failure and Handover Failure Log Reporting.' Defines timing accuracy requirements for logging handover failure events. Note: this clause records handover failures; it does not define A3 event thresholds, hysteresis, or the handover algorithm itself.
rows.causal_mechanism: A faulty handover algorithm causes the UE to trigger handovers too frequently (ping-pong effect) based on incorrect A3 event thresholds or misconfigured hysteresis parameters. Frequent handovers cause oscillating RSRP readings as the UE alternates between cells. UL_SNR and UL_BLER spike during each transition. Packet loss occurs during the handover gap. The handover procedure is defined by 3GPP RRC specifications, while in the O-RAN architecture a Near-RT RIC/xApp may participate in mobility optimization or policy control depending on the deployed E2 service model. The Near-RT RIC mapping is an architectural control-plane mapping, not a claim that 3GPP assigns handover control exclusively to the Near-RT RIC.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Handover parameter control (A3 event thresholds, hysteresis, time-to-trigger) may be managed by Near-RT RIC xApps via the E2 interface in O-RAN deployments. The KG contains Near-RT RIC traffic steering, cell reselection/handover parameter adjustment, and E2 control procedures. This is an architectural mapping.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC to E2 Node, handover parameter control); O-RAN.WG2.A1 (A1 interface, RIC policy from Non-RT RIC)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains HANDOVER REQUIRED, HANDOVER REQUEST, Handover Notify, conditional handover (condHandover-r16), handover failure (condHandoverFailure-r16), Handover Failure Log Reporting, Relative Time Stamp Accuracy, N1-to-N1 handover, X2AP handover procedures, and Dual Active Protocol Stack from TS 38.133, TS 38.523, and TS 32.423.
rows.notes: Support class corrected from Directly supportable to Mechanism-level. TS 38.133 §4.3.5 is confirmed but covers timestamp accuracy for failure log reporting, not the handover algorithm. TS 38.331 added as secondary reference for RRC handover procedure clauses.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.5 (Out-of-band blocking — receiver performance under out-of-band interference caused by filter degradation) + TS 38.141-1 §7.6 (Receiver spurious emissions) + TS 38.104 §6.6 (Unwanted emissions — transmitter spurious emissions caused by faulty RF filter stopband failure)
rows.clause_text: §7.5 Out-of-band blocking: defines the minimum requirement for receiver performance in the presence of an out-of-band interfering signal. §7.6 Receiver spurious emissions: defines limits for spurious emissions from the receiver port. TS 38.104 §6.6 Unwanted emissions: defines requirements for out-of-band and spurious transmitter emissions, distinguishing out-of-band emission limits from spurious emission limits.
rows.causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.
rows.oran_component_rationale: RF filters are physical components located in the O-RU RF chain. Both the receiver filter and the transmit filter are O-RU hardware components.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (Fronthaul interface, O-RU RF chain management)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains OTA out-of-band blocking (TS 38.141-1 §7.5), receiver spurious emissions (§7.6), out-of-band blocking co-location requirements (TS 38.104 §4.9), OTA in-channel selectivity, and receiver blocking/selectivity requirements.
rows.notes: CLAUSE NUMBER CORRECTION from v1.0: §7.6 was incorrectly labelled out-of-band blocking. Correct mapping: §7.5 = Out-of-band blocking; §7.6 = Receiver spurious emissions. TS 38.104 corrected from §6 to §6.6 (Unwanted emissions). Both confirmed in Rel-19.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — static congestion reflects a sustained traffic overload condition already at saturation level; PRB utilization is high from the start of the anomaly window rather than building up.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 (DL Total PRB Usage) + TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.2 (UL Total PRB Usage) + TS 38.314 §4 (Layer 2 measurements)
rows.clause_text: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 DL Total PRB Usage: 'This measurement provides the total usage of downlink Physical Resource Blocks (PRBs) expressed as a percentage of the total available PRBs.' §5.1.1.2.2 UL Total PRB Usage: same definition for uplink. TS 38.314 §4 Layer 2 measurements: defines measurements performed at Layer 2 including PDCP/RLC throughput and buffer occupancy metrics.
rows.causal_mechanism: Static high network congestion occurs when sustained traffic demand exceeds the available radio resources in the cell. PRB utilization in both uplink and downlink reaches saturation (near 100%). With all PRBs allocated, the scheduler cannot serve additional UEs or increase throughput, causing TX_Bytes to plateau and Estimated_UL_Buffer to grow. DL_MCS and UL_MCS may drop as the scheduler is forced to serve cell-edge UEs. Distinguished from Buffer Overflow by the cell-wide PRB saturation pattern versus UE-specific buffer growth.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler responsible for PRB allocation runs in the O-DU. Congestion is fundamentally a scheduling resource exhaustion problem at the O-DU layer.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC load balancing xApp via E2)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: TS 28.552 Rel-19 V19.6.0 explicitly defines §5.1.1.2.1 as DL Total PRB Usage and §5.1.1.2.2 as UL Total PRB Usage including percentage of PRBs used. TS 38.314 Rel-19 V19.0.0 explicitly defines §4 as Layer 2 measurements. This is the strongest measured-by mapping in the table.
rows.notes: Upgraded from §5 (too broad) to §5.1.1.2.1 + §5.1.1.2.2 confirmed in TS 28.552 Rel-19 V19.6.0. Evidence strength upgraded from MEDIUM to HIGH.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — PRB utilization rises as a traffic burst accumulates and recovers after the burst clears. Unlike static congestion, the overload condition builds and subsides rather than being sustained from the start.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 (DL Total PRB Usage) + TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.2 (UL Total PRB Usage) + TS 38.314 §4 (Layer 2 measurements)
rows.clause_text: Same as Row 8 — §5.1.1.2.1 DL Total PRB Usage and §5.1.1.2.2 UL Total PRB Usage from TS 28.552 Rel-19 V19.6.0; §4 Layer 2 measurements from TS 38.314 Rel-19 V19.0.0. The temporal/static distinction is in the TelecomTS anomaly injection model, not in the governing specification.
rows.causal_mechanism: Temporal high network congestion occurs when a traffic burst causes PRB utilization to surge and then subside. PRB utilization rises sharply during the burst, causing Estimated_UL_Buffer growth, TX_Bytes drop, and MCS degradation. After the burst subsides, metrics recover. Same governing standards as Static Congestion; the temporal/static distinction is in the anomaly injection model.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Same as Static Congestion — MAC scheduler at the O-DU is the primary component managing resource allocation under temporal load surges.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC load balancing xApp)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: Same KG evidence as Static Congestion. The temporal distinction is in anomaly behavior (TelecomTS injection model), not in the governing 3GPP specification.
rows.notes: Same clause corrections as row 8. Shares governing clause with Static Congestion — separated because TelecomTS defines them as distinct anomaly types with different temporal behavior and potentially different SHAP rankings.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5 (MAC procedures; scheduling and resource-allocation procedures — parent clause defining correct scheduler behavior that the bug violates)
rows.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5 MAC procedures: parent clause covering uplink and downlink resource allocation, dynamic scheduling, HARQ processes, and Buffer Status Reporting procedures. 3GPP does not define 'resource allocation bug' as a fault label — §5 specifies the intended MAC behavior that the software anomaly violates. Exact scheduling subclause (candidate: §5.4.3.1.3 UL resource allocation or §5.3.1 DL assignment) to be confirmed from Rel-19 PDF.
rows.pdf_action_required: Confirm exact Rel-19 TS 38.321 scheduling subclause (candidate: §5.4.3.1.3 for UL resource allocation, §5.3.1 for DL assignment) and replace §5 parent reference with the specific subclause. Source: 3gpp.org/ftp/Specs/archive/38_series/38.321/
rows.causal_mechanism: A resource allocation bug in the MAC scheduler at the O-DU causes inconsistent or suboptimal PRB assignment. Unlike congestion (where PRBs are exhausted by demand), a scheduler bug may leave PRBs underutilized while some UEs are starved. DL_MCS and UL_MCS fluctuate erratically rather than tracking channel quality, and UL_BLER rises because incorrect MCS selections are made. Distinguished from congestion by the absence of PRB saturation.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
rows.notes: Support class corrected from Directly supportable to Mechanism-level. §5 retained as parent clause only — exact subclause pending PDF confirmation. 3GPP does not define 'resource allocation bug' as a fault label; §5 specifies the correct behavior that the bug violates.

jamming_note.reason: Jamming is a physical RF attack with no corresponding 3GPP Technical Specification clause. 3GPP standards define legitimate network behavior and do not govern adversarial jamming. When the classifier predicts Jamming, the alignment table returns no result and the dashboard displays: 'No 3GPP standard applicable — this is a physical RF attack. Historical ticket retrieval only.'
jamming_note.pipeline_fallback: Layer 3 uses ticket-retrieval evidence only for Jamming predictions. SHAP chart and fault label are still displayed normally.
